Disease Outbreak Disrupts Power Sector Operations in Ghana

A disease outbreak has led to significant disruptions across the Electric Utilities industry in Ghana, with Electricity Co Of Ghana Ltd among the companies currently affected. The outbreak, identified as a highly contagious respiratory illness, has been reported at multiple power generation and distribution sites since late last week.

Industry officials say that over 120 workers have tested positive so far, resulting in staff shortages at key substations and power plants. "We have implemented emergency protocols, including shift changes and quarantine measures, but the impact on daily operations has been unavoidable," said Kojo Mensah, spokesperson for Electricity Co Of Ghana Ltd. "Some routine maintenance schedules have been delayed, and we are prioritising essential supply routes to minimise service interruptions."

A spokesperson for the Ghana Utilities Workers Union, Esi Abena, expressed concern about the safety of frontline staff. "Employees are anxious. We urge all companies to provide additional protective equipment and support for affected workers and their families," Abena stated.

The Volta Grid Power Company, another operator in the sector, confirmed temporary closures at two of its facilities, citing precautionary measures to prevent further spread. Electricity supply to some residential areas in Accra and Kumasi has already faced brief interruptions, though officials insist efforts are underway to restore full service as soon as possible.

The Ghana Power Industry Association has called for urgent government assistance, including medical support and expedited testing for all sector employees. As the situation develops, officials have assured the public that contingency plans are in place to maintain critical electricity services.
